questions.q: Why does the lesson say AI service costs deserve extra attention compared to typical Azure resources?
options: Because price per token varies enormously by model, and usage can spike quickly from bugs or retry loops
Because Azure Cost Management doesn't support AI resources at all
Because AI services are always free
Because AI services can only be billed annually
questions.explain: A frontier model can cost many times more per token than a smaller model, and bursty usage (like a retry loop or bug) can spike spend within minutes.

questions.q: What does Cost analysis let you do with AI service spend?
options: Only see a single subscription-wide total with no detail
Drill from the subscription level down to the specific resource generating a charge
Automatically cancel any resource over budget
Predict exact token counts before a model is even deployed
questions.explain: Cost analysis lets you expand from subscription to resource group to an individual resource's product meters, pinpointing exactly where spend is coming from.

questions.q: What is the main benefit of setting a budget with an alert on a resource group holding an AI deployment?
options: It automatically reduces your Azure bill
It permanently disables the resource
It notifies you of a runaway cost while there's still time to react, rather than finding out at invoice time
It removes the need for any further cost monitoring
questions.explain: A budget with an alert threshold catches a runaway deployment (bug, retry loop, leaked key) early, rather than only discovering the problem on the monthly invoice.

questions.q: What does the accumulated costs view help you distinguish?
options: The programming language used by a deployment
The physical location of the Azure datacenter
The number of employees on your team
Whether spend is climbing steadily (normal growth) or spiking suddenly (likely a bug or incident)
questions.explain: The shape of the accumulated costs line matters: steady growth is normal, while a sudden step-change usually signals something worth investigating.

questions.q: According to the lesson, why should you watch token usage specifically, not just total dollars spent?
options: A model swap changes your cost per call even if call volume stays the same
Token usage has no relationship to cost at all
Tokens are billed separately from the AI service entirely
Watching tokens is required by law
questions.explain: Because price per token varies by model, swapping which model powers a deployment changes your cost per call even without any change in how many calls you make.
